sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Recall Checkpoint 1! During an FDA regulatory audit of a medical imaging model, the file mammography_clean_v3 dot parquet on the training cluster has a different SHA-256 hash than the compliance vault file bearing the exact same filename. What happens to the audit, and how must the system be redesigned? Select your answer on the slide!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Both files have the exact same filename 'mammography_clean_v3.parquet', Dr. Nova! Does a different SHA-256 hash automatically invalidate compliance?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In regulated MLOps, filenames mean nothing! Select the correct architectural diagnosis on the card below!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! The regulatory audit is invalidated because provenance is broken. Because mutable filenames can be silently overwritten, production systems must enforce Content-Addressable Storage verified via DVC SHA-256 digests prior to every training run!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Careful! Identical filenames never guarantee identical training bytes. When cryptographic SHA-256 hashes diverge, regulatory provenance is completely broken and model certification fails!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: We have docked at the Dynamic RBAC Column Masking and Crypto-Shred Workbench! Use the controls directly above me to switch between System Administrator, ML Research Engineer, External Auditor, and Anonymous Public access, inspect DVC commits, or execute a live GDPR Article 17 cryptographic purge on Patient 002!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the table when I toggle ML Research Engineer! Direct identifiers like Patient Name and SSN prefixes are masked out automatically while preserving clinical features!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Now try clicking External Auditor to inspect age binning for k-anonymity, or toggle the GDPR Article 17 Crypto-Shred switch!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Recall Checkpoint 2! A European user demands GDPR Article 17 deletion of ten thousand voice clips already used to train a one-point-two-million-dollar foundation speech model. How should dataset management architecture enable compliant machine unlearning without repeating the entire million-dollar pretraining run? Select your answer on the slide!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Ten thousand voice clips baked into a one-point-two-million-dollar foundation model! Surely we cannot afford to retrain the entire model every time a single user invokes GDPR!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Choose the exact partitioned sharding architecture below that slashes unlearning compute costs by ninety percent!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding architecture diagnosis! Using partitioned dataset sharding—known as SISA: Sharded, Isolated, Sliced, Aggregated—isolates constituent samples into independent sub-models. Deleting a user only requires retraining the single shard containing their clips, cutting unlearning compute by ninety percent!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Merely deleting files from storage leaves gradients memorized inside neural weights. Only partitioned dataset sharding, SISA, permits surgically retraining one isolated slice without repeating the million-dollar run!
